documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: HPI:
57 yo F presents with 4 days of fever, productive cough with rusty sputum, R-sided pleuritic chest pain, and progressive dyspnea.
Reports subjective chills and rigors last night, poor oral intake today, lightheaded on standing.
Denies hemoptysis, leg swelling, calf pain, recent travel, or sick contacts other than grandchild with URI.
Brought in by daughter for increasing confusion this morning - pt intermittently disoriented to place per daughter.
PMH: type 2 DM, HTN, remote 20 pack-year smoking history, quit 12 yrs ago.
Home meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
ED course / Vitals:
Triage: T 38.9, HR 118, BP 86/54, respiratory rate 32, SpO2 87% on RA.
Hypotension to 86/54 at triage; 2 L normal saline given; BP after fluids 96/58.
Placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%; respiratory rate 30 at 4 hours (14:20).
Exam:
Gen: ill-appearing, mildly confused, answers slowly. Oriented to self and year of birth only.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes. Neck supple.
Resp: tachypneic, accessory muscle use, bronchial breath sounds and crackles R mid and base, dullness to percussion R base.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no JVD. Cap refill 3 sec.
Abd: soft, nontender. Ext: no edema. Skin warm, no rash.
Data:
WBC 18.6 with 88% neutrophils, Hgb 12.1, plt 244. BUN 34, Cr 1.3, Na 132, K 3.6, glucose 216, lactate 2.8.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion.
Blood cultures x2 and sputum Gram stain/culture sent; strep/legionella urinary antigens sent.
Assessment/Plan:
57 yo F with severe community-acquired pneumonia, RML/RLL, with hypoxemic respiratory failure, sepsis physiology, and acute confusion. CURB-65 of 3.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED plus azithromycin 500 mg IV; admit to stepdown for close monitoring.
Continue 3L NC, titrate for SpO2 >92%; q4h vitals; repeat lactate; hold lisinopril and metformin; SSI for glucose; incentive spirometer, OOB with assist.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD2
lines: Admitting diagnosis: severe community-acquired pneumonia with hypoxemia and sepsis physiology.
Discharge diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia, RML/RLL, with small right pleural effusion; resolved acute confusion; resolving AKI.
Hospital course:
Admitted from ED where triage SpO2 87% on RA; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%. Respiratory rate 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours.
Hypotension to 86/54 at triage; 2 L normal saline given; BP after fluids 96/58. No vasopressors required.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to stepdown.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. Effusion small, not tapped.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED; tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime the next morning, with azithromycin continued.
HD2 06:40 - afebrile x18h, T 37.1, HR 88, BP 112/68, RR 20, mentation back to baseline per daughter. Cr down to 1.0, WBC 12.4, lactate 1.4.
Blood cultures no growth at 24h. Sputum with mixed flora. Urinary antigens negative.
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2; ambulated hallway with RN at 11:15, saturations maintained 92-94% on 3L, pt declined further weaning trial this shift.
Home oxygen 2-3L NC arranged with delivery to home prior to discharge; RT provided teaching on tubing, concentrator, and no-smoking precautions with pt and daughter.
Discharge meds: cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID x5 days, azithromycin 250 mg daily x3 more days, resume metformin and atorvastatin, hold lisinopril x3 days then resume if BP >110 systolic.
Home O2 as above with pulse oximeter and instructions to call if saturation <90% at rest.
Follow-up with primary care in 3-5 days for reassessment and oxygen weaning; repeat chest imaging in 6 weeks given smoking history.
Return precautions reviewed: worsening dyspnea, fever >38.5, confusion, chest pain, or inability to keep fluids down.
Discharged home with daughter at 15:30, ambulatory, stable on 3L NC.
